newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire opposition rejects Speaker, waits for Kabila.
newsitem.headline: Zaire opposition rejects Speaker, waits for Kabila.

text.p: Zaire's radical opposition has rejected the election of Archbishop Laurent Monsengwo as Speaker of parliament and a possible interim successor to President Mobutu Sese Seko, spokesmen said on Sunday.

"It was a piece of theatre and an operation which we are ignoring completely. It is an affair that concerns Mobutu's followers who want Monsengwo to save Mobutu," Mukendi wa Mulumba, a close adviser of radical opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi, told Reuters.

"Monsengwo is a Mobutist. We cannot chase Mobutu and keep another Mobutist at the top. We will make his life hard -- he will not be able to work easily," Laurent Mbayo, another Tshisekedi spokesman and adviser, told Reuters.
Mukendi reiterated the militant opposition's support for rebel leader Laurent Kabila, whose forces control most of Zaire' vast territory and are closing in on the capital Kinshasa.
"The AFDL (Kabila's rebel forces) are for change. Our militants have supported Kabila across the country and we have asked them to welcome him here in Kinshasa too," Mukendi added.
Lawmakers elected Monsengwo Speaker of parliament on Saturday, urging him to take a negotiating position between Mobutu and Kabila in order to safeguard democratic changes.
The vote was marred by a walkout by radical opposition parties allied to Tshisekedi.

The popular archbishop of the northeastern city of Kisangani arrived in Brazzaville on Monday by plane from Brussels and went for a meeting with members of the Congolese church. He gave no statement at the airport but family members said earlier he would return to Zaire on Monday or Tuesday.
Mbayo said the radical opposition would call for a "ghost town" stay-at-home protest on Wednesday this week should Monsengwo return to Kinshasa to accept the post.
Tshisekedi's UDPS party has aligned itself closely to Kabila's rebels, calling on soldiers loyal to Mobutu to lay down their weapons and allow rebels to enter Kinshasa peacefully.
"For a long time we have been calling on the military not to fight Kabila. Now the 4,000 or so soldiers fighting for Kinshasa are not even our own soldiers," he said.

Diplomats and sources at the presidency say UNITA soldiers from Angola are fighting alongside the Zairean army around 200 km (120 miles) east of Kinshasa where the rebel advance has run into resistance.
